In 7-dimensional [[geometry]], there are 95 [[uniform 7-polytope|uniform polytopes]] with D<sub>7</sub> symmetry; 32 are unique, and 63 are shared with the B<sub>7</sub> symmetry. There are two regular forms, the [[7-orthoplex]], and [[7-demicube]] with 14 and 64 vertices respectively.

They can be visualized as symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s in [[Coxeter plane]]s of the D<sub>6</sub> Coxeter group, and other subgroups.
__TOC__

== Graphs ==
Symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s of these 32 polytopes can be made in the D<sub>7</sub>, D<sub>6</sub>, D<sub>5</sub>, D<sub>4</sub>, D<sub>3</sub>, A<sub>5</sub>, A<sub>3</sub>, [[Coxeter plane]]s. A<sub>k</sub> has ''[k+1]'' symmetry, D<sub>k</sub> has ''[2(k-1)]'' symmetry. B<sub>7</sub> is also included although only half of its [14] symmetry exists in these polytopes.

These 32 polytopes are each shown in these 8 symmetry planes, with vertices and edges drawn, and vertices colored by the number of overlapping vertices in each projective position in progressive order: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, red-violet.
